qa.verdict: Spec is READY for dev. All 4 NB blockers from Round 3 (NB7-NB10) are resolved. Comprehensive consistency check and Codex adversarial review found no new blockers. 2 new warnings added (W7, W8). All prior warnings (W2-W6) carried forward as non-blocking.

codex_consult.feedback_summary: Codex raised 3 BLOCKER findings and 6 WARNING findings. After independent source verification: (1) BLOCKER-1 /api/save envelope not specified — reclassified as out_of_scope: the envelope (trip_id, day, editor_session, mutations) is already implemented in the existing template at lines 1883/1923; dev is removing EDITOR_MODE guards, not rebuilding save logic; editorSession generation ternary at line 1883 is covered by M1 (remove all EDITOR_MODE guards). (2) BLOCKER-2 route status 'error' not covered by AC12/AC23 — downgraded to WARNING (W7): route.py verified to return {status: 'error'} on Gaode call failure; AC23 covers 'unknown' and 'network error' but not server-returned 'error' status; could cause silent no-feedback on Gaode failures but does not prevent core functionality. (3) BLOCKER-3 export failure ambiguous — downgraded to WARNING (W8): export endpoint always returns HTTP 200 verified; AC26 defines success as 'response.file_path present' which implicitly defines failure; gap is that developer checking resp.ok would always show success. Codex warnings 4-9 evaluated: W4 offline/navigator.onLine — M6/AC6 correctly specify event-based handlers with initial state from navigator.onLine; implementation detail. W5 resolver canonical function — maps to existing W6. W6 droppable state + compatibility — AC22 independently prevents drops on missing/skipped slots via data-droppable=false; no gap. W7 budget stale guard — maps to existing W3. W8 AC1 verification — maps to existing W4. W9 approved state for later stages — no stages after user-selected exist in save.py STAGES; M8 'or later' is safe defensive phrasing.
codex_consult.feedback_incorporated: Codex BLOCKER-1 reclassified as out_of_scope (existing code handles save envelope). Codex BLOCKER-2 added as new warning W7. Codex BLOCKER-3 added as new warning W8. Codex warnings 4-9 mapped to existing warnings or confirmed as non-issues after source verification. 0 new blockers from Codex. 2 new warnings from Codex.

NB1.evidence: M11 (ticket line 113) now reads: 'display route-unknown text and retry button when status===unknown OR the request fails (per M23); discard responses with stale request_seq only'. The old 'ignore stale/unknown/error responses' clause is gone. M11 now aligns with M23 and AC12/AC23.

NB2.evidence: Technical Hint 12 (ticket line 532) now reads: 'returns a new object with the source key present and set to null (NOT deleted — absent key falls back to persisted value under AC10 hasOwnProperty semantics) and the destination key set to the option_id, in one functional update call'. The 'source key deleted' wording is replaced with 'source key present and set to null'.

NB3.evidence: AC19 (ticket line 378) now reads: 'resolved via the shared AC10 hasOwnProperty resolver... the raw slot.selected_option_id field MUST NOT be checked directly'. M19 (ticket line 121) also updated: 'using the shared AC10 hasOwnProperty resolver, equal to option_id; a null resolved value means explicitly deselected and the raw slot.selected_option_id field MUST NOT be checked directly'.

NB4.evidence: AC7 (ticket line 270) now reads: 'THEN ConflictBanner appears (same unconditional requirement as the 409-soft case above; generic save error state is for all other non-2xx responses only)'. The parenthetical '(or save error state is shown)' is removed; ConflictBanner is now mandatory for HTTP 409.

NB5.evidence: AC24 (ticket line 430) now explicitly handles absent key: 'GIVEN a day where at least one key in REQUIRED_SLOT_KEYS is either (a) absent from effectiveDay entirely (missing state per AC22) OR (b) present but not skipped and has no selected_option_id'. The 'if the slot exists' exemption is explicitly prohibited. Hint 19 (ticket line 546) now says: 'if the slot key is ABSENT from effectiveDay (missing state per AC22) → not all filled (counts as unfilled, disables Approve); The if the slot exists exemption MUST NOT be applied to required slots'.

NB6.evidence: AC11 (ticket line 300) now reads: 'WHEN any selection-changing save completes successfully — candidates→plan drop, plan→candidates deselect, slot→slot move, or tap-to-select — and POST /api/save returns 200'. All four selection-changing directions are now explicitly covered.

blockers.title: AC5 does not exclude HTTP 409 from the error save state — contradicts M5's explicit exclusion
blockers.description: M5 (ticket line 107) says: 'error on network failure or non-OK responses other than HTTP 409 (HTTP 409 is handled by ConflictBanner per M7 — it does NOT trigger the error save state)'. M5 is unambiguous: HTTP 409 must NOT set the error save state. AC7 (line 270) was fixed in NB4 to require ConflictBanner unconditionally for HTTP 409. However AC5 (ticket lines 250-253) still reads: 'shows error if the POST returns non-2xx or network error'. HTTP 409 is non-2xx. AC5 does not exclude it. A dev implementing strictly from AC5 would set error save state for HTTP 409 (violating M5's 'does NOT trigger the error save state'). The only spec text that excludes 409 from error state is M5 — but ACs are where dev implements tests. The AC layer must carry the exclusion explicitly.

evidence.m5_text: error on network failure or non-OK responses other than HTTP 409 (HTTP 409 is handled by ConflictBanner per M7 — it does NOT trigger the error save state) (ticket line 107)
evidence.ac5_text: shows 'error' if the POST returns non-2xx or network error (ticket line 252) — does NOT exclude HTTP 409
evidence.ac7_text: ConflictBanner appears (same unconditional requirement as the 409-soft case above; generic save error state is for all other non-2xx responses only) (ticket line 270)
evidence.conflict: M5 and AC7 both say HTTP 409 must NOT trigger error save state. AC5 says error for any non-2xx, which includes 409.

blockers.proposed_fix: Update AC5 line 252 to: 'shows error if the POST returns a network error or a non-2xx response other than HTTP 409; HTTP 409 shows ConflictBanner per AC7 and does NOT set the generic save error state'.

blockers.title: AC26 export gating does not explicitly include absent required-slot key (missing state) as a disabled condition — same class as NB5 for Approve
blockers.description: AC24 was fixed in NB5: it now explicitly states that a required slot key ABSENT from effectiveDay counts as unfilled and disables Approve. AC26 (ticket line 463) says: 'GIVEN the user is offline OR any non-skipped slot in REQUIRED_SLOT_KEYS is unfilled across ANY day'. The phrase 'unfilled' could be read as 'present but with no selected_option_id'. A day where accommodation is absent from effectiveDay entirely (missing state per AC22) would pass AC26's check literally — the absent slot is not a 'non-skipped slot that is unfilled' because there is no slot object to check. AC24 now has an explicit '(a) absent from effectiveDay entirely' clause; AC26 does not. This creates an inconsistency: export buttons would remain enabled when an accommodation slot is missing from a day, while the Approve button would correctly be disabled for that same day.

evidence.ac26_text: any non-skipped slot in REQUIRED_SLOT_KEYS is unfilled across ANY day (ticket line 463) — no explicit absent-key case
evidence.ac24_fix: absent from effectiveDay entirely (missing state per AC22) counts as unfilled (ticket line 430)
evidence.conflict: AC24 explicitly covers absent key; AC26 does not. Export buttons could remain enabled with a missing required slot.

blockers.proposed_fix: Update AC26 line 463 to: 'GIVEN the user is offline OR for any day, any key in REQUIRED_SLOT_KEYS is either absent from effectiveDay (missing state per AC22) OR present but not skipped and has no resolved selected_option_id — WHEN the buttons render — THEN both Export buttons are disabled'. Mirror AC24's exact formulation.

blockers.title: AC6 only tests OfflineBanner visibility — M6's 'saves skipped/marked error when offline' has no acceptance criterion
blockers.description: M6 (ticket line 108) requires: (1) OfflineBanner shown when offline, (2) saves skipped/marked error when offline, (3) no background queue/retry. AC6 (ticket lines 255-262) tests: (a) OfflineBanner appears on offline event, (b) OfflineBanner disappears on online event, (c) no background save retry queue. M6's requirement (2) — saves are proactively skipped before attempting the POST — has no THEN clause in AC6. A dev could implement: offline event → show OfflineBanner → save attempt still fires /api/save POST (which fails due to network) — and pass all AC6 assertions while violating M6. The distinction matters: M6 says saves should be proactively skipped (not just fail after), and should mark the save status as error/offline before any network attempt.

evidence.m6_text: saves skipped/marked error when offline; no background queue/retry (ticket line 108)
evidence.ac6_gap: AC6 has no THEN clause for: WHEN user performs a save-triggering action while offline, THEN no /api/save POST is sent AND save status is marked error/offline
evidence.consequence: Dev could show OfflineBanner correctly but still fire POST when offline — passes AC6, violates M6.

blockers.proposed_fix: Add to AC6: 'AND WHEN the user performs a save-triggering action (drops a candidate, clicks approve, etc.) while offline THEN no /api/save POST request is made AND the save status indicator shows error or offline state AND no background queue is created to retry later'.

blockers.title: M10/AC11 say 'response day_total' (top-level field) but actual /api/budget/recompute returns days[].day_total — runtime undefined reference verified from source
blockers.description: AC11 (ticket line 302) says: 'the displayed day total is updated from the response day_total field'. M10 (ticket line 112) says: 'update displayed day total from response day_total'. The actual /api/budget/recompute endpoint (scripts/lib/server/budget.py:181-187) returns: {schema_version, trip_id, trip_total, currency_local, days: [{day: N, day_total: X, breakdown: {...}}]}. There is NO top-level day_total field. The day total is in response.days[0].day_total (or response.days.find(d => d.day === requestedDay).day_total). A dev implementing AC11 literally would write: displayedTotal = response.day_total — which is undefined at runtime. This is a runtime bug that makes the budget recompute feature silently show nothing (undefined renders as empty/NaN). Verified directly from scripts/lib/server/budget.py lines 181-187.

evidence.ac11_text: the displayed day total is updated from the response day_total field (ticket line 302)
evidence.m10_text: update displayed day total from response day_total (ticket line 112)
evidence.actual_response: scripts/lib/server/budget.py:181-187 returns {schema_version, trip_id, trip_total, currency_local, days: [{day: N, day_total: X, breakdown: {...}}]} — no top-level day_total
evidence.runtime_effect: response.day_total is undefined; correct access is response.days.find(d => d.day === requestedDayNumber)?.day_total

blockers.proposed_fix: Update AC11 THEN clause to: 'the displayed day total is updated from response.days.find(d => d.day === requestedDayNumber)?.day_total where requestedDayNumber is the integer day number passed in the request body'. Update M10 to: 'update displayed day total from response.days entry matching the requested day number (response.days[].day_total)'. Add Edge Case note: 'BudgetResponse.days is always an array; when a specific day is requested, response.days contains entries for all days but trip_total is the only top-level total; look up by day number, not array position 0'.

warnings.title: Mobile breakpoint boundary ambiguity at exactly 768px — AC13 does not specify boundary-inclusive behavior
warnings.description: M12 says isMobileLayout = window.innerWidth < 768. AC13 tests at 390px (mobile) and 1440px (desktop) but does not specify what happens at exactly 768px. A dev implementing with <= instead of < would pass all specified test widths but produce different behavior at the boundary.
warnings.proposed_fix: Add AC13 boundary test: 'GIVEN viewport width = 767px, THEN mobile layout active. GIVEN viewport width = 768px, THEN desktop layout active.'

warnings.title: Budget recompute stale-response guard scope (per-day vs global) unspecified
warnings.description: M10/M25 specify 'same stale-response guard (request_seq)' without clarifying whether request_seq is global or per-day. Both implementations are functionally acceptable; this is an implementation detail, not a spec contradiction.
warnings.proposed_fix: Clarify AC25: 'The stale-response guard is per-day (each day maintains its own monotonic request_seq for budget recompute)' or state global. Either is acceptable.

warnings.title: AC1 verification command does not actually generate trip HTML bytes
warnings.description: AC1's WHEN clause runs serve-trip.py --help and imports generate_html — it does not generate and grep the actual HTML output. QA will need to use a real curl or browser check against /trip/<id> to verify EDITOR_MODE is absent from generated HTML.
warnings.proposed_fix: Replace AC1 verification command with a real HTML generation check: generate HTML and grep the output bytes.

warnings.title: M16 is absent from MoSCoW list with no explanation — numbering jumps M15 to M17
warnings.description: Requirements are numbered M1-M15 then jump directly to M17. No M16 exists. Full reactive re-render is covered by M15 and AC16; no functional requirement appears missing. This is a traceability gap: any tooling checking MoSCoW coverage by ID would flag M16 as absent. Codex classified as OBSERVATION_ONLY.
warnings.proposed_fix: Add placeholder after M15: 'M16: intentionally unused — full reactive re-render covered by M15; AC16 maps to M15.' Or renumber M17-M29 as M16-M28 for contiguous IDs.

warnings.title: AC22 required-empty state says 'no selected_option_id' without clarifying raw vs resolved value — effectiveDay construction semantics unspecified
warnings.description: AC22 says required-empty styling when slot has 'no selected_option_id and not skipped'. After editorSelections[key]=null (explicit deselect via drag-to-candidates), the raw slot.selected_option_id on persisted day data is still non-null. The question is whether effectiveDay construction propagates the null resolution into the slot object's selected_option_id field (making AC22's raw check correct) or not (making AC22 wrongly show the slot as filled). Codex classified OBSERVATION_ONLY on the reasoning that effectiveDay derives all content through the resolver. The spec does not explicitly state how effectiveDay's slot objects are constructed.
warnings.proposed_fix: Add to AC22 or M22: 'the required-empty determination uses the resolved selected_option_id from the shared AC10 hasOwnProperty resolver — if editorSelections[dayKey+:+slotId] is null (explicitly deselected), the slot is treated as having no selected_option_id for required-empty purposes'.
